Frontend regex `/^(sk-|bbk_)/i` mirrors backend exactly — single source of truth would be nicer (config endpoint exposing the pattern) but cosmetic.

DEFAULT_EMERGENT_MODEL='claude-sonnet-4-6' is a non-dated short name. The emergent client appears to accept that directly. If Emergent ever requires a dated suffix, the fallback chain in call_emergent (claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929) provides safety net. Good.

rca_of_the_issue: User-reported bug: Test Connection returned 'AI service temporarily unavailable' AND a copy of an Emergent API key (sk-emergent-dDaA292Ef6fAa5e3aB) was visible in the Model field. Root causes: (1) Hardcoded model id 'claude-sonnet-4-5-20251101' did not exist in Emergent's catalog (correct dated id is -20250929); since the emergent client logged failure and called fallback which was ALSO the broken id, both paths failed → generic 'temporarily unavailable' surfaced. (2) Model <input> had no autoComplete prevention → browser autofill / clipboard suggested an API key string. (3) No server-side guard against API-key-shaped values reaching the dispatcher. Fixes verified live via curl + pytest + Playwright: (a) Test Connection now returns {success:true,response:'pong'} for emergent with null model and with model='claude-sonnet-4-5'. (b) PUT with sk-* or bbk_* model → 400 with detail 'Model must be a model name (e.g. claude-sonnet-4-5), not an API key.' (c) UI shows red warning + Save shows toast. Reproduction is no longer possible — both layers reject the bad input.
